title: Productivity Protocol contract
description: The platform-neutral contract for one protocol. A protocol.yaml (or .json) that validates against this schema and satisfies the structural kernel checks is STRUCTURALLY conformant with the Verified Agent Work kernel — its required fields are present and its steps are mapped. Structural conformance is not semantic fidelity (a validator cannot confirm a model actually follows the steps) and says nothing about benefit: see productivity_evidence for the separate, evidence-backed benefit claim.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record targets.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier, unique in the registry. Never reused for a different protocol.

version.description: Semantic version of this protocol. Bumped on any change to procedure, permissions, or acceptance tests.

purpose.description: One or two sentences: the task this protocol addresses and the deliverable it promises. Kernel step 1.

assurance_level.description: The kernel assurance level, set by the risk of the work. Determines which kernel steps are mandatory.

use_when.description: Conditions under which this protocol is the right tool.

do_not_use_when.description: Conditions under which this protocol must not be used. A protocol with no stated non-uses is under-specified.

required_inputs.description: Kernel step 2: what the agent works on.

expected_outputs.description: Kernel steps 1 and 8: what is handed back.

required_capabilities.description: Model/runtime capabilities the protocol needs (e.g. file-read, long-context, tool-use). Kernel step 3.

optional_tools.description: Optional external tools/MCP connections. Each must state how the protocol degrades without it.

permissions.description: Least-privilege grants. An action not listed here is not permitted. Kernel step 3.

prohibited_actions.description: Actions that must never occur, stated explicitly even when obvious. Kernel step 3. Never inferred from the permission set.

human_checkpoints.description: Points where a person must approve before the agent proceeds. Kernel step 4. Placed before irreversible or outward-facing actions.

procedure.description: Ordered, verifiable checkpoints. Kernel steps 5 and 6.

acceptance_tests.description: Explicit tests the deliverable must pass. Kernel step 7. At least one positive and one failure/boundary test are required by the validator.

stop_conditions.description: Conditions under which the agent must stop and surface rather than proceed. Kernel step 7.

failure_modes.description: Known ways this protocol goes wrong, with detection and mitigation. Kernel step 4.

privacy_class.description: The most sensitive data class the protocol may touch.

risk_class.description: Worst plausible outcome of a bad run. Drives the assurance level.

tested_models.description: Models the protocol has actually been run against. Empty is honest; a fabricated entry is a defect.

assurance_status.description: Where the protocol sits on the protocol-assurance ladder. Structure/testing/security — NOT benefit.

productivity_evidence.description: Where the protocol sits on the productivity-evidence ladder. Benefit — measured, never assumed. Independent of assurance_status.

retest_triggers.description: Events that invalidate the current verification (e.g. model deprecation, tool API change).

last_verified.description: ISO date of the most recent successful verification run.

license.description: Dual licence: CC0 for prose/templates, Apache-2.0 for scripts/validators.

content.description: SPDX id for prose/templates, e.g. CC0-1.0.

code.description: SPDX id for scripts/software, e.g. Apache-2.0.

evidence_role.description: Whether this input may be used to justify claims (kernel step 2).

degraded_without.description: How the protocol still works, at reduced assurance, without this tool.

resource.description: What the access applies to (e.g. supplied files, working directory).

scope.description: Breadth of the grant. 'broad' requires explicit justification and raises the risk class.

before.description: The action that must not proceed without approval.

check.description: How this step is verified when it completes.

statement.description: What must be true of the deliverable.

kind.description: positive: it does the right thing. negative: it does NOT do a wrong thing. boundary: it behaves at an edge case.

automated.description: Whether tools/validate.js or a script can check this without a human.
